The exact signed distance function is derived by projecting the point onto the plane of the torus ring and computing the distance to the center of the tube [S6].

The claim states that the signed distance function for a torus is derived by projecting a point onto the plane of the torus ring and computing the distance to the center of the tube. The provided text from Source [S6] explicitly defines the torus as 'the product of two circles' and provides the formula d(x, Torus) = ||(||(x, y)|| - R) - r|| (represented in the OCR text as d(x, ¹) = E(E(x, y)E!R, z)E!r, which corresponds to the standard analytical solution for a torus centered at the origin aligned with the z-axis). This mathematical formulation is geometrically equivalent to projecting the point (x, y, z) onto the xy-plane (the plane of the torus ring), calculating the distance from the origin to that projection (||(x, y)||), subtracting the major radius R to find the distance to the center of the tube's cross-section, and then subtracting the minor radius r to find the distance to the surface. Thus, the evidence supports the geometric description in the claim.
